prompt: Now the second biome, same locked painterly style. FOREST BIOME, ISLE PORTRAIT. It must read clearly different from the Roothold isle: wilder, denser and darker, a canopy so thick the sky is hard to see, not a sacred grove. A single representative wild Forest sky isle floating above a sea of cloud, in three-quarter view from slightly above, so we see its top, its lip and its full underside tapering to a point into the clouds. Landscape image. Mood: deep, quiet, a little dangerous; dappled golden light at the sunlit edge, then dark shadowed glades under the canopy. Top: dense pine and birch woodland with a few old-growth giants rising above them, and one Duskcrown yew with red and violet leaves glowing softly; the canopy covers almost the whole top. Ground: needle and leaf litter, ferns, moss, exposed roots, deadfall; brambles, fallen logs, stumps, clusters of mushrooms; a brook winding to a still dark pool; no paths, no tending. Lip: rocky mossy edge with fallen trunks jutting over it and roots and ferns hanging off; the brook spills off the lip as a small waterfall. Underside: dark mossy stone (darker and blacker than the Roothold granite), with a couple of holes pierced right through the rock showing sky beneath, roots and moss hanging from it, tapering into the cloud. No buildings at all. One small human figure at the forest edge for scale. Painterly game concept art, not photoreal, no text.
